### Step 6 — Review

Three questions are read at every rigor — `evidence` · `adversarial` · `structure` — each by the one independent reader `SKILL.md`'s rigor table deals it. The auditor falsifies the *evidence* and never reviews the code; the critic and the reviewer falsify the *code*. A reader is never the author nor a fork of the orchestrator, and is shown no other reader's verdict. Its brief names its questions on a line of its own, `Questions: <q>[, <q>]`, exactly the set the plan's rigor deals its role, or the dispatch wall refuses it; and nothing of their checks: `payload/context/checks-<question>.md` is delivered to it at start, and a paraphrase is a weaker second source. It writes one record per question it is dealt, and its brief lists every record on `Files:`, `Expected artifact:` naming one of them. The reader dealt `evidence`, whichever role holds it, declares one to three runs in all, suites under `Suites:` and other runners under `Re-executes:`; `Suites: none` with no `Re-executes:` is for a reader not dealt `evidence`.

**Each landing is read.** A read row is a `review` row whose `reads` carries `live:head:<q>[+<q>]`; exclusivity, range and return-to-pending are per question. It is ready for each landed difference its questions have not read, and its reader reads that range (`scope: piece`).

**The whole read, once.** At `scale: wave` each code question also owes `scope=whole`, read once the last build row has landed, in the one batch `steps/5.md` dispatches; it reads across pieces, never each piece again.

**The read after a fix.** A fix gets one read per owed question, over the range the tick prints for its row and the plan rows and criteria it names. A row confirmed at an earlier head and not named is not read again.

**The record and its fact.** Each record is a file under `record/` with flush-left lines `reviewed: <a>..<b>`, `question: <q>`, `result: <pass|flag|fail>`, `scope: <piece|whole>`; for `structure`, one line `check: <id> <PASS|FLAG|FAIL|n/a> <reason>` per check id. When the reader's roster row carries `severity` in `pushed=`, the record also holds `findings: <n>`, one `finding: <n> <S1|S2|S3|S4> <on|off> <path>:<line>|- <title>` per finding, `shown: <n> <command>` for each finding the table sends to fix and `unsure: <n> <what is not known>` for a finding that owes a check (`payload/context/severity.md`); it writes no priority, and one that does is refused when it differs from the table. Otherwise a record with no `findings:` line registers with `result:` as written. Register it with `session-poker.sh proof-add review <record> --question <q> --reader <name>`, `<record>` spelled `record/…` from the docs root or as an absolute path: the head is the record's `b`; the reader's role is read from its roster row, never typed. Code past a question's last head is uncovered for that question.

**A finding the reader cannot settle owes a check, and a move is the user's word.** An `unsure:` line makes its finding a check owed, a `check:` line on the plan. A check record under `record/`, naming its `written-by:` agent (neither the finding's reviewer nor the code's writer), settles it with `session-poker.sh finding-check <record>#<n> settled <S> <reach> | refuted | unsettled <check record>`, and `current 8` waits on every open one. `session-poker.sh finding-move <record>#<n> <defer|fix> '<the user's words>' '<why>'` moves a finding across the line, on the main thread only, and only on words the user typed in a prompt of this session: at least three whole words, or their whole prompt. A pasted block, a tool result and another agent's text are not theirs, and an S1 is never deferred. A record path registers one pass; the `check:`, `deferred:` and `moved:` lines that bind a finding belong to that pass, so a later pass is written to a new record path.

**The waiver is the user's.** `session-poker.sh waive <question> '<reply>'` writes `waived: question=<q> head=<40-hex> by <git user.name> <ISO-UTC> "<reason>"`, covering that question up to that head. An agent never waives.
